sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2021. Change Request 2021-027 (split of [lno] Lango into Imotong, Logir, Okolie, Lango) + Request for New Language Code Element [oie] Okolie, dated 2021-08-09.
sources.note: Nothing. Identity, population (~16,000 Ketebo+Lorwama), location (Losite payam, Ikotos county), closest language Dongotono [ddd]; 'no written literature'; only source cited is Muniru 2019.

sources.citation: Muniru, John. 2019. Sociolinguistic assessment of Lango, Imotong, Logir, Okolie (Lorwama and Ketebo) and Dongotono speech varieties of Torit State, South Sudan: A summary of findings. Juba: SIL South Sudan. 8 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 91877).
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey only (200-item wordlist lexicostatistics, RTT, EGIDS, attitudes). Gives autonym Okolie [òkólíɛ̀], Ketebo [kɛ̀tɛ́bò], Lorwama [lòɾwámá]; Ketebo~Lorwama 90% lexically similar, next closest Dongotono 46-47%. No prosody statement.

sources.citation: Simonse, Simon. 2018 [1992]. Kings of Disaster: Dualism, Centralism and the Scapegoat King in Southeastern Sudan. (archive.org scanned text).
sources.note: Nothing (ethnography). Useful negative witness: 'Dongotono, including the dialects of the Imotong, Ketebo, Logir, Lokwa and Lorwama. I am not aware of scholarly research on the relationships between these different dialects.'

sources.citation: Vossen, Rainer. 1982. The Eastern Nilotes: Linguistic and Historical Reconstructions (Kölner Beiträge zur Afrikanistik 9). Berlin: Reimer. -- Rosetta Project excerpt for Dongotono [ddd], pp. 165-166.
sources.note: Nothing on Okolie; excerpt is informant notes for Dongotono/Lokoya. Vossen collected no Ketebo/Lorwama data (his Lotuxo-group languages are Lotuko, Lopit, Dongotono, Lokoya).

sources.citation: Muratori, Carlo. 1938. Grammatica Lotuxo. Verona: Missioni Africane. (archive.org full scanned,../otuh1238/) -- Introduzione and 'Sguardo sintetico sul linguaggio Lotuxo' pp. 464-473: remarks on Dongotono and Lorwama, comparative word tables, and a Lorwama fable text supplied by P. Barbisotti.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage KF 21547 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Nothing on Lorwama/Ketebo accent. Says Dongotono and Lorwama are mutually intelligible, not intelligible with Lotuxo proper, lack the Lotuxo gender prefix, show Acoli lexical influence. Muratori's accent section (sec. 49, p. 18) concerns Lotuxo proper only.

sources.citation: Driberg, J. H. 1932. Lotuko dialects. American Anthropologist n.s. 34(4): 601-609 (doi 10.1525/aa.1932.34.4.02a00060), read in the whole-volume scanned of AA 34 (Digital Library of India scan on archive.org).
sources.note: Nothing. Short comparative vocabularies of Lotuko-group varieties; Lorwama mentioned only in a footnote as a branch of the 'Lango' round Ikoto extending to Madial and Madi Opei; no Ketebo/Lorwama vocabulary, no prosody.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page okol1243 (classification Eastern Nilotic > Lotuxo > Lopit-Dongotono > Dongotonic; MEDs = Flores 1971, Driberg 1932) and Wikipedia 'Ketebo people' / 'Dongotono language' pages.
sources.note: Nothing; Wikipedia Dongotono page reproduces Vossen's joint Dongotono/Lopit/Lokoya consonant inventory only.

sources.citation: Flores, Joseph. 1971. A simple introduction to the Ketebo or Mening language with vocabulary. Naporo: Catholic Church Karenga (Karamoja, Uganda). 84 pp.

sources.note: The only descriptive work on the language recorded by Glottolog (MED = grammar_sketch); a missionary primer of this kind often has a pronunciation/accent note. Likely held only in Comboni/Catholic mission archives (Karenga, Moroto, Verona/Rome) or in the private collections behind Glottolog's 'hh' bibliography.

sources.citation: Muniru, John et al. (SIL South Sudan). Full survey report and 200-item wordlists (Lango, Imotong, Logir, Okolie-Lorwama, Okolie-Ketebo, Dongotono), fieldwork June 2019 -- underlying data of the 8-page summary (SIL archives 91877); any subsequent SIL South Sudan Okolie orthography statement / alphabet workshop materials (post-2021).

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. 1981(b), unpublished/limited-circulation notes cited by Mann & Dalby 1987 (A Thesaurus of African Languages) as describing Ketebo (Lokathan area) and Napore as languages 'with a Lotuxo base'; cf. Tucker & Bryan 1956/1966 Lotuho unit ('LORWAMA (LOWAMA), around Madial').

sources.note: Only other linguist's first-hand characterisation of Ketebo found; Tucker & Bryan 1966 (Linguistic Analyses) has a Lotuho stress/tone paragraph that may mention dialects. Archive.org copy of T&B 1966 is lending-only.
